invariants: Actual pinned DeepSeek Fetch and the selected native adapter retain POST body on 307/308 and rewrite POST on 301/302/303; PUT and HEAD boundaries have separate actual raw Fetch/shared-carrier observations.
Authorization, proxy authorization and cookies disappear across origin changes and do not return when redirecting back. Attribution headers persist; body header removal follows actual method rewrite.
Twenty redirects are admitted; the twenty-first redirect and repeated-URL loop fail as transport errors after exactly twenty-one requests.
Observed credential-bearing or unsupported-protocol targets refuse without another request; relative path/query space/fragment and Host override observations match actual pinned Fetch.
An owned abort before follow admits no target; a response with unfinished redirect body does not block reaching the target. Previous response and all owned transport resources close on termination.

All twenty-nine complete ordered Source/native/extracted observation objects and imported runtime module hashes must match fresh Source identity. Error prose and full transport protocol are outside this bounded contract.
identity: Fifteen actual adapter cases and fourteen actual pinned raw Fetch/shared carrier cases; request origin index, method/path, selected headers, JSON body, terminal chunks/status/error and candidate module closure.
ownership: Clone the initial Request rather than mutating its caller; close the old redirect response before following through the same owned connection/cancellation machinery.
ordering: Apply rewrite and sensitive-header removal before target admission; bound the whole redirect chain with one count and preserve retained body bytes.
errors: Observed invalid target/count failures are URLError at the carrier and TRANSPORT at the adapter; controller cancellation remains ABORTED. No original bug predicates are broadened.
cancellation: The current owned signal/idle checks govern each follow-up connection and read; explicit pre-follow abort and unfinished redirect-body observations are required.
adaptation: Python3.8 stdlib owned HTTP/HTTPS handlers receive a Fetch-compatible redirect handler; no product Node, frontend modifications or external credentials.
open_questions: Full WHATWG URL/IDNA/unicode, TLS, proxies, all compression/framing, authentication and every provider route remain separate transport contracts.
Complete Tools/Wire/profile combinations, general JS, overall migration and deferred real Win7 remain unaccepted.

rc1_review.scope: Current finite executable provider/consumer corpora, original-browser and extracted observations in the single full receipt. Historical alpha evidence remains historical; no inventory-wide parity, arbitrary ABI/history, paid-provider or Win7 certification.
